items.statement: Targets 55.4 million tons production and sales for FY26, equal to full EC capacity
items.quote: Around 55.4 million tons is what we are targeting. This is the EC capacity -- max EC capacity that we will have. Both the production and sales, we are trying to reach that.

items.statement: Aspirational target to reach 55 million tons in FY26 by running plants at 95-105% capacity
items.quote: That's an aspirational target we also understand because our plant capacities will have to be worked at around 100%, 102%, 105% -- some of the plant at 105%, some of them at 95%.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected around INR4,000-4,200 crores; INR40,000 crores sanctioned by mid-year; INR31,000-32,000 crores at drawing board
items.quote: This year, FY '26, most of the efforts would be on sanctioning the works and getting them off the ground. So actual capex would be -- we expect around INR4,000 crores this year.

items.statement: INR28,000-29,000 crores already sanctioned; INR12,000 crores more to be sanctioned in couple of months; INR2,000 crores under partnership model
items.quote: Sanctioned is about INR28,000 crores, INR29,000 crores. Another INR12,000 crores will be sanctioned in a couple of months. So you can take sanctioned by July or August, is around INR40,000 crores.

items.statement: Plan to grow from ~50 million tons to ~100 million tons in next 3-4 years; major capacity jump expected FY29-30
items.quote: This is the first year in the block of 4 to 5 years where we plan to take NMDC from 50 million tons approximately to about 100 million tons.

items.statement: KK line doubling 131 km, only 20 km left in two sections; completion targeted by end of FY26
items.quote: Only two sections are left out of 131 kilometers, 20 kilometers is left. One is Kamalur to Bhansi, other is Bhansi to Bacheli. Rest of them has been completed.

items.statement: Nagarnar steel plant targeting 2.6-2.7 million tons HR coils in FY26 (~98% capacity utilization)
items.quote: We will be doing this year around 2.6 to 2.7, which is about 98% capacity utilization of HR coils. That will do.

items.statement: Pellet export target 2.5-3 million tons in FY26 (full KIOCL capacity) vs 0.5 million tons in FY25
items.quote: This year, our target is to do 30 lakh tons or 3 million tons, which is the full capacity of the KIOCL plant.

items.statement: Expects $30-50/ton premium on DRI-grade pellets (66-67% Fe) vs current 62-63% grade at $105-110/ton
items.quote: If we are selling high grade, this average will go up to around $140 to $150 as per the current market situation.

items.statement: Nagarnar turned EBITDA positive monthly in March-April 2025; cash collection rose to INR1,400-1,500 crores/month
items.quote: Back of the envelope calculation also shows that we have become EBITDA positive on a monthly basis on March and April.

items.statement: Receivables INR7,800 crores mainly from RINL and NSL; both now paying ~INR200 crores/month; expects significant reduction by FY26 end
items.quote: Both these outstanding accounts have become active in terms of liquidation of the outstanding. So going forward, by the end of this year, you will see a much truncated number.

items.statement: Domestic capex largely internally funded; debt decision for overseas acquisitions in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: One more calculation, we can expect most of it would be internally financed, but whether we should -- considering our expansion plans beyond India, one call has to be taken about a year from now or about 1.5 years from now.

items.statement: Actively evaluating coking coal assets abroad (Indonesia, Australia, others); prefers operational stage assets; Board-sanctioned policy for 10 minerals
items.quote: We are actively looking for assets abroad and we are evaluating many, many assets, which obviously cannot be discussed in the public domain.

items.statement: Rohne coal block targeting operational by Q3/Q4 FY26; Section 9 notification pending; animal corridor issue resolved
items.quote: Rohne should get operational by the end of this financial year. I think we have already done Section 5 and the Section 7 notification for Rohne has already been done.

items.statement: Started index-based pricing pilot for iron ore; aims for automated, frequent, multi-point pricing for 100M ton distributed business
items.quote: We are trying to come into index-based or a formula-based pricing. That's the first time we did last month after 3, 4 months of research.

items.statement: 60% of Nagarnar HR coil sales routed through SAIL stock yards on user-charge basis; 40% direct
items.quote: Currently, because we thought that creating depots everywhere is a very expensive and time-consuming in a different way. So we have entered into arrangement with SAIL. And I think 60% of our total sales as of date is routed through SAIL.

items.statement: Lloyds Metals expansion not a major threat; only competes in Raipur region (<10% of NMDC sales); market size growing for all
items.quote: No, I don't think Lloyds is a competition for us in the -- their competition -- a little competition for us at the Raipur area. But Raipur for us accounts for around 4 million tons of ore only.

items.statement: Nagarnar techno-economics improved: coke rate 530, PCI 150, fuel rate 530, PRP 15 MW; ran blast furnace at 10,000-11,000 tpd vs 9,650 rated
items.quote: Our coke rate is around 530 right now. Fuel is around 530 -- fuel rate is 530. And now in April and -- March and April, we have touched a PCI rate of 150.

items.statement: NMDC CMDC JV iron ore and coal blocks expected operational in FY26
items.quote: We hope that this year would be the year where our new assets like the two coal blocks and the two iron ore blocks under our JV, NMDC CMDC Limited should also become operational.

items.statement: EC applications: Bailadila 55-60M tons, Karnataka 17M tons, Deposit 4 (7M tons) FSC meeting held, Deposit 13 (13-18M tons) transfer pending
items.quote: We have applied for this EC in Bailadila for NMDC, would be around 55 million tons only in Bailadila and -- 55 million to 60 million tons. And I think 17 million tons in the Karnataka sector.

items.statement: Gold Legacy project stabilized in last 2-3 months; expects profitability in FY26 after first-year losses
items.quote: And we have also stabilized Legacy in the last 2 months, 3 months. And hopefully, in this financial year, Legacy would also be showing us good profits.

items.statement: Dubai office opened to coordinate African asset evaluation
items.quote: But the good thing is that we have been able to open an office at Dubai so that our Africa -- the assets that we look at -- are looking in Africa is easily coordinated.

items.statement: Domestic iron ore prices stable at INR99-102/t for weeks; HRC segment strong, non-HRC (sponge) slightly down
items.quote: If you see it's been hovering around INR99 to INR102 only for the past several weeks. So there has been some sort of a stability coming in.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR3,700 crores (highest ever); PAT up 19% YoY, PBT up 16% despite 43-44 lost production days
items.quote: We have seen that the capex was the highest this year, which was INR3,700 crores, highest ever. And we plan to continue much higher capex.

items.statement: Energy vertical EBIT contribution expected to increase significantly in FY26 with full year of 600 MW thermal plant operations and improving PLF
items.quote: The energy vertical between hydropower and thermal power, has already contributed almost 50% of EBIT, earnings before interest and tax in FY'25 and this contribution is expected to increase further in FY'26 with the full year of operation of the 600 megawatt thermal power plant and the improving PLF.

items.statement: No forward volume guidance given for steel and power; production expected to return to normal FY24 levels with potential improvement from modifications
items.quote: Normally, we don't give forward guidance, but I mean we have taken modifications and we expect things to be because the plant will now be operational and with a better efficiency so things should be better, but in terms of numbers we don't give forward-looking guidance.

items.statement: 50 MW captive solar plant commissioning expected in current financial year; 30 MW TG set replacement operations expected by mid FY27
items.quote: Captive Solar Plant (50 MW)- Execution is delayed due to the issues at the end of the EPC contractor that is Gensol. Most equipment s have been delivered and transmission line work is going on. Project commissioning is expected in current Financial Year. 30 MW TG set replacement - Work is on schedule with operations expected to begin by mid FY'27.

items.statement: Rehar Hydropower 25 MW trial run complete, commercial operations to commence when water flow improves, PPA expected to be finalized this quarter; Kotaiveera 25 MW work expected to begin by mid FY26
items.quote: Rehar Hydropower Project (25 MW ) - The trial run of the plant is complete . Commercial operations will commence when water flow improves. The PPA is expected to be finalized this quarter. Kotaiveera Hydropower Project, 25 MW - The project is in the approval stage wit h work expected to begin by mid FY'26.

items.statement: Ferroalloy pricing expected to see 5% depression mainly due to ore price reduction; domestic demand strong but export demand stressed due to tariff issues
items.quote: Ferroalloys pricing wise, we will see probably a 5% depression mainly, but this is going to be mainly caused by the reduction of the ore prices more than anything else. Demand wise, demand we think domestic demand is going to be quite good , strong. Export demand is going to be a little stress because of these tariff issues

items.statement: Net consolidated debt below Rs. 1,600 crores; cash and liquid investments exceed Rs. 1,250 crores; long-term loans repayable within next year Rs. 235 crores
items.quote: Net consolidated debt including working capital loans stood below Rs. 1,600 crores. Long-term loans repayable within the next year amount to Rs. 235 crores. Liquidity remains strong on the balance sheet with cash and liquid investments exceeding Rs. 1,250 crores

items.statement: Exchange power prices fell 70% in FY25 to Rs. 4.31 from Rs. 5.17 in FY24; declined 10% YoY in Q4
items.quote: Exchange power prices fell by 70% in FY'25 to Rs. 4.31 from Rs. 5.17 in FY'24 and declined by 10% YoY in Q4.

items.statement: Indian coal index declined 14.56% and coking coal prices softened, partly offsetting margin compression; government incentives for underground mining introduced
items.quote: The Indian coal index declined by 14.56% and coking coal prices also softened, partly offsetting margin compression. The central government has introduced incentives for underground mining, including upfront fee waivers, reduced performance guarantees and lower minimum bid prices.

items.statement: SKS Power consumes ~10,000 tons coal/day at full capacity; utilizing SHAKTI coal linkages, captive commercial coal mines, and third-party coal
items.quote: Sir, every day if the plant is running at full capacity, we are consuming 10,000 tons of coal, generally I am just giving you thumb rule on how the consumption is happening. So government comes out with SHAKTI coal linkages and the coal prices are much much cheaper.

items.statement: SKS Power expansion environment clearance lapsed; need to redo public hearing; all clearances expected in 1-1.5 years before starting process
items.quote: Sir, regarding the power plant expansion in SKS Power, so we had an environment clearance, but it has lapsed. So, we have to again redo the public hearing and things like that. Our team is gearing for it and in the coming one year or 1.5 years, we will have all the clearance and then we can start the process.

items.statement: Indian coal production crossed 1 billion tons in FY25, growing 5%; coal imports fell 9%, saving US$6.93 billion forex
items.quote: Indian coal production crossed 1 billion tons in FY'25, growing by 5%. Coal imports fell by 9%, saving US $6.93 billion in Forex.

items.statement: Export demand unpredictability due to global tariff issues and safeguard investigations; ferroalloy export demand stressed
items.quote: Export demand is going to be a little stress because of these tariff issues and safeguard investigations everything going on all over the world. There is a little unpredictability about the export demand scenario. It is a little tough.

items.statement: FY26 targets: 5.2-5.5 msf sales volume, Rs 3,000-3,300 cr sales value, ~Rs 1,800 cr collections, 3,300+ unit handovers, 8-10 project completions, 4 msf delivery, 7-8 msf new pipeline addition with ~Rs 5,000 cr GDV
items.quote: Around 5.2 to 5.5 million square feet of sales, 3,000 to 3,300 crores of sales value, roughly about 1,800 odd crores of collection, 3,300 plus units to be handed over. All this completions will come from 8 to 10 projects that are scheduled for completion, and we will be delivering another 4 million square feet next year.

items.statement: Medium-term mission targets by FY28: Rs 5,000 cr annual sales value, 7.5-8.0 msf annual sales volume, Rs 2,500-3,000 cr revenue, Rs 250-280 cr earnings
items.quote: We are trying to achieve a mission target of about Rs. 5,000 crores of sales value by FY'28. Revenues of around Rs. 3,000 crores or between Rs. 2,500 to Rs. 3,000 crores. And an earnings of around Rs. 250 to Rs. 280 crores, all by FY'28.

items.statement: Ongoing projects: 19.2 msf total, 15.7 msf sold (8.0 msf recognized, 7.7 msf unrecognized), 3.5 msf unsold inventory; new project pipeline: ~17 msf unlaunched
items.quote: As you are aware, we always talked about our ongoing project pipeline, roughly about 19.2 million square feet is t he ongoing projects. Out of which , 15.7 million is sold, 3.5 million is not yet sold

items.statement: Revenue recognition potential from ongoing projects: Rs 5,000+ cr total sales value over next 36 months; own/JDA: 6.1 msf for Rs 3,100 cr revenue; JV: Rs 1,800 cr revenue (profit share only)
items.quote: And the unsold inventory of 3.5 million square feet in our portfolio can also be sold in less than a year's time based on our current run rate, which means 11.2 million square feet of area ongoing projects will be available for revenue recogniti on over the next three years. And they carry a sales value of roughly about Rs. 5,000 plus crores

items.statement: JV projects gross margin ~20%+ currently; early phases lower margin (20-25%), later phases higher; overall project target 25%
items.quote: Gross margin should be somewhere around 20% plus. Jitendra Gupta: Okay. Gopalakrishnan J.: It's a slightly low margin business. At least the phases that we recognize now, I will give you some color on it. Two joint ventures have come into revenue recognition, first phases of two projects have come into revenue recognition mode

items.statement: Average price increase ~3% across portfolio in FY25; completed projects saw higher appreciation; expects 5-7% annual price growth going forward, sufficient to cover construction cost inflation
items.quote: At SPL, we witnessed an average pric e increase of around 3 % across our portfolio in FY '25. Notably, projects nearing completion or already completed witnessed relatively high appreciation. This reinforces our belief in maintaining price discipline while ensuring volumes and absorption remains healthy

items.statement: Strong demand in mid and mid-premium segments (74% of CY24 sales); SPL focused on these segments for volume, lower volatility, and brand strength; affordable segment de-emphasized
items.quote: We observed consistent demand in the mid and mid-premium housing segments. SPL's strategic pivot in recent years towards this segment has proven to be the right move. As I mentioned a short while ago, industry-wide launches remain subdued throughout the FY'25, primarily due to regulatory bottlenecks.

items.statement: FY25 free cash flow Rs 273 cr; invested Rs 143 cr in new projects; net free cash flow Rs 130 cr; cash balance Rs 320 cr; 3-year cumulative free cash flow Rs 545 cr, invested Rs 365 cr
items.value: Rs 273 cr FCF; Rs 143 cr invested; Rs 130 cr net FCF; Rs 320 cr cash
items.quote: We generated free cash flow of Rs. 273 crore in FY25 against Rs. 156 crores in FY'24. Against this strong free cash flow generation, we invested Rs. 143 crore towards new project commitment and thus finished the year with net free cash flow of Rs. 130 crore, leaving us with the cash and cash equivalents of Rs. 320 crore at the end of the year.

items.statement: Net debt reduced 26% to Rs 326 cr; debt/equity 0.24x (from 0.35x); WACC 11.3% (from 11.6%); comfortable max 0.5x debt/equity; may temporarily exceed for land acquisition
items.value: Rs 326 cr net debt; 0.24x D/E; 11.3% WACC
items.quote: Our net debt is down approximately to Rs. 326 crores and reduced our debt equity ratio from 0.35% in FY'24 to 0.24 now, reflecting a strong and more balanced capital structure. The cost of fund remain ed stable with weighted average cost dropped marginally to 11.3 % in FY'25 compared to 11.6 last year

items.statement: To secure 15-20 msf new pipeline needs Rs 1,500-2,000 cr land cost; JDA model reduces capital need to Rs 600-700 cr; SPL contribution Rs 500-600 cr; Rs 350-360 cr from operations over 24-30 months; may use bridge borrowing
items.quote: To lock this 15 million square feet that we are talking about, we are talking about a land commitment, assuming you buy all of these lands, it will cost you between Rs. 1,500 crores to Rs. 2,000 crores. If we do majority on JDA, we don't need to bring that kind of money. The capital commitment required to secure this will be somewhere around Rs. 600 crores to Rs. 700 crores of capital.

items.statement: FY25 launches: 3 new projects + 3 new phases = 2.6 msf (below target); deferred launches now cleared: Pune launched Q1 FY26 (125 units in 48 hrs), Bangalore targeting June 2025 launch; FY26 target 7-8 launches including these
items.quote: Despite the regulatory delays and launch deferments, SPL launched three new projects in FY'25, one each in Bangalore, Chennai, and Kolkata. Also, we launched three new phases in existing projects, one in Bangalore and two in Chennai. All launches add s up to 2.6 million square feet of saleable area during F Y'25.

items.statement: Pune entry: Superstar project launched Q1 FY26, 125 units sold in 48 hours, 400+ walk-ins; plan 2-3 projects in Pune over next 12-18 months; Mumbai entry later after Pune stabilization
items.quote: We have successfully launched our Pune project under the code name Superstar in Exciting Market. We are thrilled to report that the launch generated an incredible response. In the first two days of the launch, we recorded more than 400 walk-ins and sold 125 units within 48 hours of launch.

items.statement: FY25 approval/OC delays in Karnataka (E-Khata, Kaveri 2.0) and Tamil Nadu; resolved by end Q4; industry-wide issue; expects smoother process in FY26; West Bengal dispute progressing, no new timeline
items.quote: The delayed approvals and OC came through, but only towards end of Q4. This pushed our launches to Q1 '26 and stressed revenue recognition to some extent, even though we recouped most of deferred revenue during Q4.

items.statement: Record collections Rs 1,484 cr FY25 (Q4: Rs 455 cr, +35% YoY, +31% QoQ); driven by handover momentum (1,396 units Q4, +119% QoQ); operating cash flow Rs 305 cr
items.quote: On the handover side, we navigated significant headwinds and delivered 9 projects involving 4.2 million square feet and successfully handed over 3,150 units, which is a new benchmark for SPL. Delivering 1,400 plus units in one quarter, that too with OC coming only towards the end of the quarter, reaffirms our internal capabilities.

items.statement: FY25: Sales volume 4.31 msf (flat YoY), sales value Rs 2,288 cr (flat YoY); Q4 sales volume 1.32 msf (+5% QoQ), sales value flat QoQ; handovers 3,150 units FY25 (record), 1,396 units Q4 (+119% QoQ)
items.quote: We achieved sales of 4.31 million square feet and sales value of Rs. 2,288 crores. Both were nearly flat, at last year's levels. Due to delays in launches led by approval constraints, we relied heavily on sustenance sales.

items.statement: Revenue recognition deferred Rs 500 cr in Q2/Q3; Q4 recouped Rs 230-250 cr; Rs 250-280 cr pending (Pristine Estate Rs 140 cr, Park 63 Rs 140 cr) to be recognized in FY26
items.value: Rs 500 cr deferred; Rs 230-250 cr recouped; Rs 250-280 cr pending
items.quote: From a revenue perspective, Mr. Pandey is showing me a pending realization of what Rs. 200 Crs as pending recognition between at least two key projects that only partly got recouped from the revenue recognition perspective. So out of Rs. 500 crores that got deferred in Q2/Q3, we realized about 230 to 250 crores. Another 250 to 280 crores is to be further recognized in these projects and the work i

items.statement: Mid-market and mid-premium focus (74% of India demand); affordable de-emphasized; luxury/ultra-luxury avoided; may have 5-10% premium/luxury projects opportunistically
items.quote: We will remain focused on mid-market and mid-premium for three reasons. 1. Reason one, when an alternative capital providing segment like stock market or others, when they tend to be volatile, we always see the volatility more prominently in the top end of the market, which is the luxury and ultra luxury.

items.statement: End-use driven demand in mid-market provides lower volatility; investment demand low; strong brand dominance in mid-market across core cities (Bangalore, Chennai, Pune)
items.quote: Third one, because it is end-use driven mostly, investment demand is very low in mid segments. Because it is end-use driven, it is driven more by a nature of economic growth and economic operation, basically the purchasing power of the common man than the investment demand and therefore mid market tend to be low volatility in this segment.

items.statement: Business development accelerated: 30+ projects under evaluation (~18 msf); 3 msf nearing closure (documentation phase); 5-6 msf advanced diligence; 10+ msf post term sheet (3-4 months to materialize)
items.quote: Towards assembling the 15-20 million square feet, we have already accelerated our BD activities. We have over 30 plus projects that are under evaluation. 3 million square feet are nearing closure where they have moved out of the due diligence phase and are in the documentation phase.

items.statement: Royalty payment ~Rs 15-20 cr/year (Rs 4-5 cr/quarter) to stop as SPL discontinues 'member of Shriram Group' tagline; promoter holding unchanged at 28%; HoldCo restructuring only
items.quote: Roughly about Rs. 15-20 crores. Rs. 4-5 crores per quarter is a royalty charge that we provide and as I answered in the previous question to another colleague on this call, I think we waiting for resolution of that and I think we believe it is aligned between us and Government of West Bengal on how to resolve.

items.statement: Quarterly volatility and seasonality to continue; execution risk on 15-20 msf pipeline addition over 18 months; regulatory risk (though easing); West Bengal dispute timeline uncertain; land cost inflation risk
items.quote: And quarter to quarter volatility will continue. Seasonality impact will continue. But we believe on a year-to-year basis, we will keep making progress and hopefully meet your expectations in the coming years.

items.statement: New CFO Ravindra Pandey joined; management team stable; no other changes mentioned
items.quote: I am joined by my colleague, Mr. Ravindra Pandey – our new CFO, who will be walking you through the presentation and then both of us will join in answering questions as you may have.

items.statement: Promoter HoldCo restructuring: no change to SPL listed entity (promoter holding 28% unchanged); royalty to stop; Shriram Properties brand to continue perpetually
items.quote: Promoter acquisition, promoter holdings getting restructured. No change from a listed Company's perspective. No material impact on SPL as its promoter holding will remain unchanged at 28%. Changes are envisaged only at the HoldCo level where two promoters who are owning, promoter holding the Shriram properties hold co. Shareholders are changing their holding among themselves and therefore it is a

items.statement: Board approved raising up to Rs 100 crore via equity or equity-linked instruments to bolster financial position, meet working capital needs and invest in equipment
items.quote: Board of Director in its meeting held today approved raising up to 100 crores through the issue of equity shares or equity linked instruments.

items.statement: Fundraise expected to close in 2-3 months; single round planned; dilution not expected to exceed 20%
items.quote: We expect to close it in next 2 to 3 months depending upon how we are going to structure it and how does Capital Bridge Advisors advices us.

items.statement: Total borrowings Rs 162 crore (long-term Rs 39 crore, short-term Rs 123 crore); utilized Rs 144 crore of sanctioned Rs 162 crore; interest cost ~9%
items.quote: The company's total borrowings stood at 162 crores. This includes long-term borrowings of ₹39 crores and short-term borrowings of 123 crores

items.statement: No plan to raise further debt; debt expected to reduce after fundraise and working capital improvement
items.quote: No. The debt is not going to be raised. Definitely there is one thing that is not going to be raised is debt.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations negative Rs 32.8 crore in FY25 due to elevated trade receivables from back-ended revenue; substantial collections expected in H1 FY26 to ease pressure
items.quote: Cash flow from operations stood at negative 32.8 crores in FY25, primarily due to elevated trade receivables, as revenues were back-ended during the year.

items.statement: Receivables increased to Rs 89 crore (includes Rs 21 crore retention money); expected to be realized by July-August and in H1 FY26
items.quote: ATCR will have a part of 21 Cr approx is of retention money. So, this ATCR comprises of 21 Cr of retention money and another 60 Cr of my actual trade receivables.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow Rs 448 crore; outstanding unexecuted order book Rs 703 crore (41% residential, 51% commercial, 8% institutional)
items.quote: In FY25, the company received orders totaling to ₹448 crores. The outstanding unexecuted orderbook was ₹703 crores.

items.statement: Order book Rs 953 crore as of May 30, 2025 after adding Arvind Aqua City (Rs 150 crore) and Nirma Corporate House (Rs 73 crore)
items.quote: The outstanding unexecuted orderbook as on May 30, 2025 is ₹953 crores

items.statement: FY26 revenue target Rs 300-350 crore; order inflow at least Rs 300 crore (bid pipeline Rs 600 crore, conversion 40-50%); execution cycle 2.5-3 years
items.quote: It's going to be between 300 to 350 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 21.6% in FY25 (up 399 bps YoY); margins expected to stay stable around current levels due to investment in skyscraper technology
items.quote: EBIDTA margins stood at 21.6% vs 17.7% last year, up 399 basis points, on a Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: PAT margin 8.0% in FY25 (up 25 bps YoY); management says margins not less than 8% TTM
items.quote: PAT margins stood at 8.0% vs 7.8% last year; up 25 basis points, on a Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs 24 crore; net block Rs 74 crore; investing in Mivan aluminium formwork (Rs 30-40 crore) and technology for 200m buildings
items.quote: In FY25, the company had incurred 24 crores. in capex. Net block as on Mar 31, 2025 stood at 74 crores

items.statement: Completed 8 projects in FY25; 30+ ongoing projects as of March 31, 2025; slab cycle reduced from 15 to 10 days for Mondel One
items.quote: In FY25, the company completed 8 projects. The no. of ongoing projects as of 31st Mar, 2025 is 30+

items.statement: Preferred contractor model: mostly negotiated awards at good margins; key clients include Arvind Smart Spaces, Nirma Limited, GIFT City developers
items.quote: We don't even have to go and tender for the projects. Most of the time what happens is even after being H1 we get awarded the project which gets us very good

items.statement: Geographical expansion to Tier-1 cities (Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Delhi) planned in 2-3 years after tri-city capacity saturated; will leverage existing client relationships
items.quote: We will move to top tier cities like Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Delhi, just in case we have expanded like in 2 to 3 years, we will be expanding and after that maybe after that we will be making our move.

items.statement: Revenue grew 8% YoY to Rs 260 crore in FY25; H2 FY25 revenue grew 4% YoY to Rs 145 crore
items.quote: Revenue from operations grew by 8% YoY to 260 crores in FY25; In H2 FY25, it grew by 4% YoY to 145 crores

items.statement: EBITDA grew 33% YoY to Rs 56 crore in FY25; H2 FY25 EBITDA grew 13% YoY to Rs 32 crore
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 33% YoY to 56 crores in FY25; EBIDTA margins stood at 21.6% vs 17.7% last year

items.statement: PAT grew 12% YoY to Rs 21 crore in FY25; H2 FY25 PAT Rs 12 crore
items.quote: PAT grew by 12% YoY to 21 crores in FY25; PAT margins stood at 8.0% vs 7.8% last year

items.statement: FY25 revenue missed estimates (Rs 261 crore vs Rs 310-325 crore) due to delays in 4 projects: Centroid (diaphragm wall failure), Nirma Hostel & Shivalik Greenfield (Rajachitthi permission delays), Orchid (cancelled over commercial negotiati
items.quote: There w ere a total four project s, one of which got cancelled and the project Centroid was delayed because of the diaphragm wall. The diaphragm wall got broken and we had to wait for at least one year

items.statement: Credit rating application planned; process to be completed by September 2025
items.quote: We have not yet applied but we will definitely go for credit rating, and we will complete it by September.

items.statement: Investing in Mivan aluminium formwork (Rs 30-40 crore) and technology for buildings up to 200m height; 7 skyscraper projects (150m) underway
items.quote: we have already taken Mivan A luminium Formwork that amounts to almost 30 to 40 Cr. As I said we are in an investment cycle currently and we have been investing a lot of money into the

items.statement: Promoters Jeet Chavda and Johil Chavda actively managing; CEO Parth Gurjar, CFO Mayank Shah on leadership team
items.quote: Joining me today on this call are Mr. Jeet Chavda – Promoter Group Member, Mr. Parth Gurjar – Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Mayank Shah – Chief Financial Officer

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of INR170-180 crore
items.quote: So, for this year, sir, we are targeting a revenue of just a tentative, I'm telling you. So, we are targeting a revenue of like INR170 to INR180 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 13% for FY25; PAT margin 9.4% for FY25
items.quote: For the financial year FY25, the revenue reached INR10,746.6 lakhs, year-on-year growth of 122.2%. EBITDA came to it at INR1,393.9 lakhs, growing 113.6% year-on-year basis. EBITDA margin stood at 13%. Net profit stood at INR1,011.7 lakhs, up to 94% growth year-on-year basis, with a PAT margin of 9.4%.

items.statement: Near-term margins expected to stay 9-10% due to expansion costs
items.quote: But the profitability is going to be similar, like between these, we are reflecting 9% to 10% in between.

items.statement: INR16 crore for Phase 1 capacity expansion to 15,500 units/month by Jan-Feb 2026, self-funded

items.quote: As we speak, our delivered order book has been refilled with new wins and at the end of the May 2025, our UK subsidiary order book stands at ₹290 crores, including old and new wins all put together.

items.statement: Order book grew 40% (INR 80 crores) from Nov 2024 to Jan 2025 reaching INR 300 crores
items.quote: We got an unprecedented increase in our order book by ₹80 crores or 40% during the period of November 2024 to the January 2025, reaching our UK subsidiary order book to the level of 300 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 20.1% YoY to INR 62.7 crores in FY25
items.quote: We clocked EBITDA of INR 62.7 crores in FY 2025 vs INR52.2 crores last year.

items.statement: UK subsidiary One of Us PAT margin improved from 6.2% in H1 to 12.6% in H2 FY25
items.quote: PAT margin of 6.2% and EBITDA percent of 11% in H1 increased to 12.6% and 15.3% in H2.

items.statement: India standalone PAT margin declined to 24.2% from 35.1% YoY due to fixed costs on lower revenue
items.quote: India standalone margin percentage updates- PAT percentage is 24.2% and EBITDA percentage is 37.3% for FY 2025. While 37.3% EBITDA margins are the healthy margin but both these percentages are lower by 10.8% and 12.8% in YoY.

items.statement: Consolidated DSO improved to 78 days from 122 days YoY due to better UK payment terms
items.quote: Moving to the next point, we made significant improvement in DSO at the console level while India DSO is still high and may take time for another two quarters to reach to the pre- strike period levels. Our console DSO - days sales outstanding improved remarkably to 78 days from 122 days in the last year.

items.statement: India collections improving, INR 18 crores collected in April-May 2025, old dues may clear by Sep 2025 or Q3 FY26
items.quote: In current year, we have already received another INR 18 crores in the month of April and May for India outstanding that is almost 80% of last year H1 collection . We expect much better collection in the H1 '26.

items.statement: Net debt of INR 8.4 crores at FY25 end vs cash surplus of INR 40.3 crores last year, used for acquisition and working capital
items.quote: Moving to the debt position, we ended the year with a net debt of INR 8.4 crores compared to the cash surplus of INR 40.3 crores last year.

items.statement: AI lab planned in collaboration with UK and India teams leveraging UK-India trade agreement R&D incentives
items.quote: We are planning to setup an AI lab in collaboration with teams in the UK and India, leveraging exceptional cross-border talent. This initiative aligns with the recently concluded UK-India trade agreement, enabling us to benefit from R&D incentives while driving innovation in VFX and production technology.

items.statement: Tech integration phase 1 completed enabling seamless cloud-based work sharing between India and London
items.quote: We have recently worked out a technical integration, which means our artists from India would connect directly to the cloud missions in London, which will allow lesser hassle in terms of sharing files and work share between India and London which would be more seamlessly.

items.statement: UK headcount grew from 290-300 to 350; India headcount up 15-20% plus freelancers
items.quote: By the time we acquired our UK subsidiary One of US, they were into the range of close to 290 to 300 employee strength. With the surge in the demand they currently stand at the 350 headcounts. Similar thing has happened in the India. India headcount has also increased by close to 15% to 20% to deliver higher volume.

items.statement: Cost arbitrage of 5-7x between India and UK employee costs for offshoring work
items.quote: If I talk about that the cost savings potentials, as I said that the difference is quite large of the expenses in India versus expense within UK, which goes to the extent from the 5x to the 7x depending upon the different category of the employees.

items.statement: Global VFX industry projected 13% CAGR to INR 147 billion by 2027 per E&Y report
items.quote: As per E&Y report, industry is now poised for strong recovery, with projections indicating a 13% CAGR through 2027, reaching INR147 billion.

items.statement: 34 global productions with budgets over USD 100M, 14 in UK/France where Basilic has presence
items.quote: Across the globe, 34 productions are being currently made with budgets exceeding USD100 million, Of these, 14 are being filmed in the UK and France, two markets where we have a direct and growing presence, especially through our acquisition of One of US and our expanding network in France.

items.statement: UK subsidiary works with premium clients Netflix, Amazon, Sony with ~30-day payment terms
items.quote: This was possible due to the better payment terms at UK subsidiary with premium clients of Netflix, Amazon and Sony.

items.statement: Acquired One of Us London (350+ artists) for INR 42 crores primary infusion, <2 year payback
items.quote: so I understand, we paid INR 42 crore the primary infusion into One of Us that was our consideration and how much has One of Us generated in EBITDA in FY '25 for us? Gaurav Mehra: Yes. I think it's 11, so if you take INR 228 crore that will be I think 18 of our total 45. Viraj: So, it should be less than a 2-year payback at the bottom

items.statement: No immediate fundraise planned but exploring balance of investment vs fundraising as opportunities arise
items.quote: I wouldn't say anything immediately, but as the opportunity comes, we are always exploring that the right balance of the investment versus fundraising.

items.statement: Key hires: Head of Studio in India, General Manager UK (Sal Umerji, 15 years experience integrating UK-India pipelines)
items.quote: we've recently hired some of the key members into our team that is Head of Studio in India and likewise we recently hired a General Manager for UK operation, Sal Umerji whoe comes from a very high level background of 15 years of experience.

items.statement: VFX industry revenue monthly phasing highly dependent on production schedules, not linear like IT
items.quote: It is important to note that VFX industry revenue monthly phasing is highly dependent on the production schedule, and it is not the likely pattern of a straight line likewise in the IT industry where we have the fixed monthly billing.

items.statement: 85% of Rotoscope and Prep/Paint work offshored to India; Compositing offshoring pending tech upskilling
items.quote: First #2 are the capabilities already existing with us and a large part of such streams offshoring havs already been moved to the India. Now for these two extremes we stand close to 85% which is delivered from India and may be 10 to 15 supervisors remain from there.

items.statement: UK production spend tripled to £632M in Q1 2025 vs £211M in Q1 2024 per BFI reports

items.statement: Consolidated revenue 3x growth to INR 306 crores in FY25 from INR 106 crores in FY24
items.quote: Happy to share that your company had outstanding growth of 3x in our console revenue for FY 2025, reaching to level of ₹306 crores from last year total revenue of ₹106 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target INR110-120 crores, 35-40% growth
items.quote: Yes. So, it could be around INR110 crores to INR120 crores is what we are targeting for the next financial year.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin around 10%, EBITDA margin around 14%
items.quote: So, around 10% would be the approximate PAT margin like last year, it was 10.1%. So, it would be around that number as per our expectations.

items.statement: FY26 volume target 16,000-17,000 units
items.quote: So, the internal volume target for FY26 would be to do about 16,000 to 17,000 units in FY26.

items.statement: H1 FY26 similar to H2 FY25, H2 FY26 slightly higher
items.quote: Yes, I mean going forward in this financial year, in H1 of FY26, we expect the numbers to be similar to what we had achieved in H2 of FY25. And H2 of FY26 is going to be slightly higher than we did in H2.

items.quote: So, we have an order book of about 1500 vehicles in the B2G segment. And we are trying to crack other B2G orders as well, as we speak.

items.quote: And currently, we have already received the LOI for 360 vehicles from a Southern India based EV rental company. And we expect a couple of more LOIs, like, I mean, we expect that we'll get a couple of more LOIs in the month of June.

items.quote: The majority of the funds like the INR21 crores 32 lakh would go into development of five new products. So, three would be in the two-wheeler category and two would be in the three-wheeler category.

items.quote: Majority will be utilized by FY26 and some portion which will be left out will be utilized by FY27.

items.statement: Imported material 6.7% of total purchases, down from ~10% last year

items.quote: 25% I would proudly say that 25% of our workforce is of engineers as of today. In the R&D team, we have about 16 to 17 R&D engineers.

items.quote: So, I was saying that your spare parts business has grown extremely well, INR17 crores now from INR7 crores last year.

items.quote: So, typically, the order cycle is about 60 days. It takes about -- after we place the order, it takes about 20 days to 25 days to make the material and about 30 days to 35 days to ship and receive it at our factory.

items.quote: Our receivables have actually technically come down on FY '20 H1 numbers. We have actually recovered, if you look at our H1 receivables, they were around at INR 42 crores. items.quote: So like I mentioned that in the next 3 to 6 months' time, we are looking at a fresh fundraise via a QIP/Rights/Preferential, and it's going to be around INR 30 crores figure. And we are going to be doing that to reduce debt primarily. So once the debt goes, the pledge gets released automatically.

items.statement: Postponed earlier planned fundraise to avoid raising capital before showing profit; will raise after Q1 profitability
items.quote: It was very easy for us to fool investors in March or in February, raise money from the market, and then announce a loss balance sheet. We had signals already that it's going to be a loss. So we are now looking at Q1, which is already looking healthy. We are going to show profit numbers, then go back to our QIP/Rights issue.

items.quote: We have our eyes and ears open. We keep seeing what's happening in the industry. And what we do believe very truly is that any VFX company that continues to ignore the threat of AI, they will have to shut shop in less than 24 months.

items.statement: Partnering with 3 international companies to automate VFX tasks (rotoscopy, cleanups, camera tracking, matchmove, compositing) using AI
items.quote: We are working alongside 3 international companies that are automating VFX tasks, which will protect us from this disruption, obviously. So we are creating tools that will use AI to automate tasks like rotoscopy, cleanups, camera tracking, matchmove, compositing.

items.quote: Yes. So, as I said previously, that it would be difficult to bifurcate both the segments by on the basis of margins, because most of the production which is done in stainless steel is consumed by elevator division.

items.statement: No export focus discussed; business is domestic B2B supplying elevator OEMs/installers across India.
items.quote: We right, like, we are not more focused on B2C, because our core is into manufacturing and we are right now focused on expanding our market reach as a B2B supplier and OEM partner only.

items.statement: Monsoon season (Q1) causes project slowdowns and lower revenue recognition despite order pipeline.
items.quote: Actually, the June quarter is weaker because of the weather conditions. Due to monsoon, majority of the projects are on a standstill, or they go slow.

items.statement: Exploring contract manufacturing for Mumbai suburban train automatic doors; technical capability exists but no orders yet.
items.quote: Ha! Mahej ji, we are already exploring into this market of contract manufacturing. So, this year we are seriously exploring that. So, if we get an opportunity, we'll surely do that.

items.statement: Stainless steel division targeting interior applications in Mumbai as new market beyond elevators.
items.quote: In Mumbai, we have seen that there is one big segment of interior application. So, we are hopeful of deploying our sheets other than elevator in the interior segment.

items.statement: Revenue potential at 80% capacity utilization of 5,000 doors/month estimated at ~Rs 200 Cr annually.
items.quote: If we look at the 80% capacity, then it will be around 200 crores, like 5,000 doors ka agar hum 80% lete hai So it will be around 200 crores.

items.statement: Management will hold earnings calls half-yearly instead of quarterly going forward.
items.quote: No, we'll be doing half yearly, only.

items.statement: Expects robust growth in AC business for FY26 but does not provide specific targets
items.quote: We do not give any like guidance. So, we cannot give target for the year. But we are expecting robust growth for this year also.

items.statement: Internal target of double-digit EBITDA margin and minimum 25% revenue growth
items.quote: No, we do not give any guidance per se, but with AC, refrigerator, etc., I think anything over 25% is a minimum for us.

items.statement: AC segment EBITDA margin expected to be minimum 5% plus in FY26
items.quote: I wouldn't like to give a range, but I would say minimum 5% plus.

items.statement: Home Appliances Division capex Rs. 100-130 crores for FY26 including washing machine 12-13kg capacity and AC
items.quote: In the appliance division CAPEX is between Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 130 crores to be spread out.

items.statement: Refrigerator production reached 50,000 units/month in recent months, targeting 55,000-60,000/month soon
items.quote: We expect very, very shortly refrigerator to stabilize at 55,000, 60,000 a month.

items.statement: Stamping division in Engineering at near full capacity (~Rs. 7 crores/month), fine-blanking can grow 15-18% with existing capacity
items.quote: I think in the stamping division we are already at capacity, by and large. Stamping division, I think capacity is Rs. 7-odd crores a month and we are like nearly there.

items.statement: Front-loader washing machine industry stagnant, up to 10kg degrowth, shift to high-end; IFB gained 1.5-2% market share
items.quote: So, the industry in front loaders has been stagnant. And overall, if you see, in the addressable market we have gained a share of around 1.5% to 2%.

items.statement: Top-loader washing machine grew 27% in Q4 vs industry 15-16%, gained 1.5-2% market share; no plans for semi-automatic segment
items.quote: In top-loaders, after the launch of the new series which we launched last year, our growth in, say, 4th Quarter was around 27% against the industry's growth of, as rightly said by you, of 15% to 16%.

items.statement: AC industry dipped ~35% in May 2025 but IFB secondaries better; expects to cover shortfall in 2-3 months
items.quote: we could see an impact in the month of May, where the indus try has dipped to the tune of around 35% odd

items.statement: Gross margins maintained despite pricing pressure; A&M cost reduction project targets Rs. 200+ crores material cost savings over 18 months, Rs. 70-80 crores P&L impact in FY26
items.quote: Out of total Rs. 200 crores cost reduction in material cost, approximately Rs. 80 crores will come in our P&L in FY '26.

items.statement: Total cost savings program across material, fixed cost, logistics/warehouse expected to exceed Rs. 350 crores, significant portion in FY26 and H1 FY27
items.quote: Our total saving from all of these should exceed, our belief is Rs. 350 crores.

items.statement: Fixed cost reduction target Rs. 6 crores/month from current Rs. 75 crores/month, starting end of Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our aim is to reduce fixed cost by Rs. 6 crores per month. Currently our fixed cost is around Rs. 75 crores per month, our aim is to reduce it by Rs. 6 crores per month, which will start coming in by end of Quarter 2.

items.statement: Freight and warehouse optimization expected to save Rs. 20 crores
items.quote: Through this project we are expecting to reduce the cost by almost Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: AC segment turned EBITDA positive in FY25 (1.7% margin); refrigerator segment turned EBITDA positive in FY25 vs loss in FY24
items.quote: It is EBITDA positive 1.7 --

items.statement: Refrigerator share of associate loss reduced to Rs. 18 crores in FY25 from Rs. 24.6 crores; expected to reduce drastically in FY26 as business turned EBITDA positive
items.quote: Share of loss was Rs. 18 crores loss, correct point, as compared to last year Rs. 24.6 crores. And refrigeration business for the FY '24-'25 has already turned EBITDA positive.

items.statement: IFB Points (exclusive stores) at 487-500 currently, targeting 700+ by end FY26, 750 by year-end; contribution to national sales increased in last 3-4 months
items.quote: Currently, we have around 487 to 500-odd stores. And our expansion plan for this financial year is to take it to around 700 plus.

items.statement: Benchmarking against LG/Samsung for dealer counter management efficiency; IFB process weak, strengthening manning and range placement town-by-town
items.quote: In LG, Samsung is very-very efficiently done, they are the only two companies which really do it well, and they are the companies we should actually benchmark in terms of efficiency of management.

items.statement: South region weak due to management vacancies, fixing in 2-3 months; North strong except UP; quality reputation helps conversion where counters manned well
items.quote: I think the region where we were historically strong but now weak because of manning issues is South. And South is the largest market, we need to do a lot, lot better in South.

items.statement: Promoting internal talent to leadership roles faster; issues with external hires; uplifting people within states to build leadership pipeline
items.quote: We are for example now uplifting people to leadership roles, even some within a state, let's say, instead of the state head. Some people we are giving part of a state etc., who have been with us for a while.

items.statement: Chain project for motorcycles must be localized in India within 1 year due to China BIS issues; possible extension
items.quote: Now with these China BIS issues etc., chain as a project will need to be brought into India. We have one year time to do this. Maybe we will get some extension also.

items.statement: Engineering division targets minimum 20% annual growth; asset turnover ratio internal guideline minimum 2.5x
items.quote: The division needs to grow by at least 20% a year, minimum, from its internal, from whatever we have now.

items.statement: Management execution risk in dealer counter manning and range placement acknowledged as prolonged issue; South region vacancies; UP market underpenetrated
items.quote: This process is weak in IFB. This process has to be strengthened, and a lot of time is going into manning properly in order to do this. Now I know we have said this quarter-after-quarter, year-after-year, but it has not happened the way it should happen.

items.statement: Targets 30-40% revenue growth annually for next two years
items.quote: So, we are targeting 30 % to 40%, anywhere between minimum 30 % to 40% growth every year for the next two years.

items.statement: Expects gross margin floor of 30% and aims to improve EBITDA margin above 10%
items.quote: Yes. Around that, means, nothing less than 30% of gross margin. 30% is going to be the bottom thing. And, yes, 10% EBITDA, we want to improve on that.

items.statement: Sees huge opportunity in mass apparel segment below ₹599 where 80-95% of market is unbranded
items.quote: So, it is around ₹20 lakhs, ₹25 lakhs crores market where 80% to 95% of the goods is being sold under ₹4 99. And then we don't have a single national brand over there.

items.statement: Women's wear bottom-wear launch in Q2 FY26; kids' wear sportswear/swimwear by end of Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our women wear is going to be launched next quarter. That is quarter two. The goods are already in production. The market research is done, and we are coming up wi th the bottom wear line for women wear

items.statement: Winter wear expanding to 300+ options with 200 in high volume for Q3 FY26
items.quote: This year, we are coming up with 300 plus options in winter wear only. And among that around 200 options are coming up with huge quantities.

items.statement: Quick commerce live on Zepto in 76 cities; adding two more platforms; targets 5-10% revenue share in a year
items.quote: We expect quick commerce to grow from zero now to 5% to 10% in in next, a year or so, and the balance will come from offline channels.

items.statement: Revenue mix target: 50-60% e-commerce, 5-10% quick commerce, balance offline and white-label
items.quote: I believe that 50 % to 60% business will come from e -commerce. We expect quick commerce to grow from zero now to 5% to 10% in in next, a year or so, and the balance will come from offline channels.

items.statement: Quick commerce margins higher than marketplace due to no returns and metro customer paying for convenience
items.quote: In quick commerce, the margins are higher. Also, the quick commerce customer is very different. It is not just the bottom of the pyramid customer. It is more of a metro customer who is okay to pay.

items.statement: Women's wear average margin better than men's; bottom-wear more stable than top-wear
items.quote: So, I believe women wear has a little better margin than men's wear. So, men's wear but if you optimise your inventory, if you optimise the products you sell, then you can obviously come down to almost similar margins.

items.statement: Asset-light model with no manufacturing capex; offline expansion via distributor network without store capex
items.quote: We are a capital light brand in both ways, in terms of manufacturing also and in terms of front end also. So, we don't have CapEx for a store to sell offline.

items.statement: Weekly procurement based on daily run-rate data; inventory split into core selling goods and small test batches
items.quote: We have since last, one , 1.5 years, we are not producing anything monthly. We are only buying weekly. So whatever sales each week is bought every week covering the period of procurement.

items.statement: Quick commerce inventory held 30-40 days with weekly replenishment; minimal working capital impact
items.quote: Among those certain number of days only, one part of the inventory goes to the quick commerce stores from where it is distributed. And we weekly replenish it. So basically, inventory over there is not going to be for more than 30, 40 days.

items.statement: No significant external capital needed; can fund growth internally or via bank cash credit if required
items.quote: If required, we can obviously arrange it ourselves or we can get some CC from bank or something.

items.statement: Offline sales concentrated in North India; online sales stronger in South India
items.quote: Our distribution is done mostly in Delhi, Punjab, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh. Also, Bengal is doing very good for us. Assam, we have just begun. Assam is doing good. So, it's more of North India, and when you go online, it's more of South India for us

items.statement: Differentiates from HRX by being casual-plus-sportswear brand with 90-95% range below ₹599 vs HRX 10-15%
items.quote: HRX is only a sportswear brand. We are a casual brand which also have sportswear, number one. Number two, HRX, target customer and our target customer are pretty different. HRX hardly has maybe 10%, 15% of its range below ₹599 and 90% to 95% of FTX range is below ₹599.

items.statement: Uses recycled yarn fabrics for cost and eco benefit; not positioned as eco-friendly brand for mass customer
items.quote: Though we use a lot of recycled fabric, recycled yarn fabric in our product line. Because again, it is eco-friendly also and it is way a little cheaper than the raw yarn.

items.statement: Return ratio 9-10%, half of industry standard; 4+ ratings on Amazon and Flipkart
items.quote: Our review ratings are also four plus, so our return ratio is also 9% to 10%, which is half of the industry standard.

items.statement: FY25 revenue ₹142-143 cr, up 26% YoY; EBITDA ₹14.23 cr; PAT ₹8.63 cr, up 71% YoY
items.quote: '24-'25, we closed at ₹142 crores, up by 26%. Our EBITDA was ₹10.82 crores, which we closed at ₹14.23 crores. Our PAT was ₹5 crores last year. This year, it was ₹8.63 crores, a growth of 71%.

items.statement: Gross margin volatility during new category launches due to experimentation with small batches
items.quote: So, whenever an introduction of new product in a fashion business, it is not like a commodity. We've never known what exactly will work. So, what we do is we experiment with smaller quantities of various designs, and then we try to figure out what is selling and what is not selling.

items.statement: Discounted sales only 1-1.5% of inventory; mainly new products without traction or platform festive promotions
items.quote: I think it is hardly 1%, 1.5% of the total inventory, which is diluted.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 600-700 crore for FY26 with potential +/- INR 100-150 crore variance
items.quote: I can tell you that 600 to 700 is guaranteed. Rest is on luck. Because if geopolitical and all other things are proper, then we will reach the projection.

items.statement: Core business revenue expected to grow 100% for next two years then 50% thereafter
items.quote: But yes, for next two years 100% I can guarantee. After that it may be 50% but 50% is also big.

items.statement: 3-4 big tenders coming for core telecom and construction business, with 2-3 more Samruddhi-like projects in pipeline
items.quote: We have 3 -4 big tenders coming for the core business. Telecom and construction. That is Kore business as of now. Entire revenue, everything is coming from that only.

items.statement: Participating in five tenders during monsoon lean season, expecting at least one success
items.quote: We are participating in five tenders. At least one will be successful. So, that will bring additional and future.

items.statement: INR 55-60 crore invested in new machinery and right of way acquisition
items.quote: It is for purchase of machines and purchase of right of way. Because my network is my asset.

items.statement: No immediate capex needed for defense; government-backed funding of INR 100 crore expected with defense project
items.quote: Once I get the defense project, along with that I will get a INR100 crores funding also, government backed.

items.statement: Telecom contributes 25-30% of revenue, roads EPC contributes 70-75%
items.quote: Sir, as a typical, normally telecom will be about 90 and rest will be from roads. About 25 % to 30% only comes from telecom.

items.statement: Diversifying into defense with deep-tech metal 3D printing; product sent for approval in 2-3 days
items.quote: We are diversifying in defense. And that is where if we are able to succeed, INR10,000 crores is just peanuts. And we are in pipeline, we are doing some product, in next 2-3 days it will be sent for approval.

items.statement: Defense procurement increased tremendously due to recent Pakistan war creating opportunities
items.quote: Plus defense development is there with the recent Pakistan war. Procurement has increased actually tremendously. And there is some opportunity.

items.statement: Samruddhi Highway opening delayed by 6 months; Mumbai-Shirdi connection expected by December
items.quote: The problem is with the opening of Samruddhi Highway which is delayed by 6 months. So, my entire project is delayed by 6 months.

items.statement: Monsoon stop-work notice received; construction speed decreases greatly during monsoon
items.quote: Already stop work notice has come. Hardik Gandhi: Okay. Ravindra Doshi: So, we will -- we have our contacts and everything, but then the speed decreases

items.statement: Trade payables increasing due to business growth; company is almost zero-debt, funded by vendors
items.quote: See, basically when work is increasing, assets are increasing, then debts are also increasing. There is nothing new about it. And then this is almost zero debt company. So, funding is done from debt only, from my vendors only.

items.statement: Almost zero-debt company; funding primarily from vendor credit
items.quote: And then this is almost zero debt company. So, funding is done from debt only, from my vendors only.

items.statement: No immediate capital raise needed; flooded with cash after Vodafone payment of INR 20 crore
items.quote: Right now it's not needed. On March we did not get the expected payment but we have we have flooded with cash. As of now. I have just Vodafone paid me INR20 crores.

items.statement: First Overseas Capital (lead manager) investigated by SEBI; no communication received by company
items.quote: First is our lead manager, First Overseas Limited was investigated by SEBI and all, but we have not received any communication regarding First Overseas till date.

items.statement: Succession plan: Managing Director's son Chaitanya will join; professional team to take over in 4 years
items.quote: For the next 4 years, I will be taking these calls. Till then, I will give you all good results. After that, the professional team will take over. After that, I will be sitting as Chairman and listening to the calls only.

items.statement: Defense orders timing unpredictable; government processes make prediction very difficult
items.quote: This is a government thing, sir. Prediction is very difficult. It will be there. That I know. We have a breakthrough. And we are in very advanced stage of producing the required spares.

items.statement: Execution speed uncertain when expanding to 3-4 states beyond Maharashtra due to state-specific issues
items.quote: Execution speed as of now I am not able to predict. But I don't foresee any serious problems which will decline our performance.

items.statement: Subsidiaries created for three business models: EPC contracting, build-and-sell, and long-term lease/annuity model
items.quote: See, basically our business runs in 2 -3 different models. One is, we only take the order, complete it and deliver forget. Second is, we take permissions from government, construct and sell it off. And third is, we take the permission, we own the project and we take revenue long term , 15 to 20-25 years, we get paid.

items.statement: Cogent Communications awaiting Government of India permission; blocked by Bharti and Reliance
items.quote: Cogent has not yet received the permission from the Government of India. Unless that comes, we cannot start. It is a very good work. But then, Bharti and Reliance both are there. So, they are not allowing it to come.

items.statement: RailTel project ongoing; Crest Digital partnership for small cell and in-building systems on Samruddhi
items.quote: Third, RailTel. Railtel is on. And the fourth is Crest Digital. Rajesh Pathak: Yes. Ravindra Doshi: Crest Digital is in the pipeline. We are on it. We are surveying

items.statement: Mumbai Metro tender lost; telecom companies creating complications reported in Times of India
items.quote: Mumbai Metro we are not successful in the tender. And after that, all the telecom companies have started creating a lot of fuss. You must have seen it in Times of India a bout Metro lines only

items.statement: Legal action against online critics attempted but abandoned; advised to ignore as time-wasting
items.quote: See when they did it first time I tried. I sent a notice. My cyber crime had actually issued them someone. Person simply ran away. And the ex-account was in the name of some peon.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target of 20% to 30%
items.quote: And this year, we are expecting somewhere around a 20% to 30% increase in the upcoming year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 12% to 13% for FY26
items.quote: Yes. Absolutely. This year, we have targeted that, the goal of ours is 12% to 13% EBITDA margin to achieve.

items.statement: 10x revenue target of ₹500 crores by FY2030 or FY2031
items.quote: So 2030 or maximum 2031, our goal is to achieve this 10x goal.

items.statement: Strong project funnel built in India and UAE with ₹10 crore and ₹15 crore pipelines respectively
items.quote: Almost in Dubai, we are having funnel of ₹15 crores. And India, we are having funnel of ₹10 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined from 13.2% to 11.8% in FY25 due to hiring and marketing spend
items.quote: But yes, definitely, percentage wise, it is decreased because of the whole activities of the hiring a new many people in the sales and experience centre and so many marketing activities we were doing.

items.statement: Motorised products nearly double ticket size vs manual blinds
items.quote: So, generally, if we look at the one blind, so this one blinds maybe let's say, if it is ₹5,000 and then motor will add ₹7,000. So it was almost a double sales value.

items.statement: Solis Motors captured 30% of motorisation mix in GCC since launch
items.quote: But now with Solis, and the launch of Solis, we already seen the shift of Solis going to 30% of the entire motorisation ratio.

items.statement: First major Solis Motors order of 900 units for a Dubai hotel
items.quote: Already since the launch, we have gotten our first big project of the Solis Motors, which is 900 motors in a hotel in Dubai.

items.statement: Strengthening production capacity and quality for expected U.S. and ROW export growth
items.quote: And over and above, we are also strengthening our production capacity as well as quality. Why this is, because considering this year, we are expecting very good export that is going to happen with the U.S. market and the other ROW market as well

items.statement: Planning Dubai experience centre similar to Mumbai centre
items.quote: Also the plan for this year is on how we've seen the experience centre of Mumbai. It is lovely all throughout, and we aim that something very, very good just like the Mumbai experience centre. We build something here as well.

items.statement: Launched Solis Motors, curtain track, and project-specific products; entered system integrator category
items.quote: We have launched Solis Motors, which is used for the blinds and curtains. We have launched curtain track as well in last year. We have added new products specially for the projects as well. We entered into new category of system integrator.

items.statement: Incorporated U.S. subsidiary with local bank account to eliminate 5% PayPal fees and import duties for customers
items.quote: So we established a USA company, and that is fully subsidiary company of USA. So last month, we did that also. Bank account was open. So now they will get the material from the local invoicing.

items.statement: Inventory days improved as percentage of sales despite new product additions; ₹50 crore inventory at ₹63 crore sales
items.quote: And last year, ₹63 crores sales and inventory were ₹50 crores. So if you see the percentage wise, it is reduced against the sales.

items.statement: ~₹2-3 crore of ₹50 crore inventory is over 5 years old; 30% of fabric designs refreshed every 2 years at 3-10% discount
items.quote: I don't have right now those data on hand. But maybe ₹ 2 crores to ₹3 crores maybe more than five years.

items.statement: Channel pricing: company cost 40%, sells to dealer at 50% of MRP, dealer sells at MRP
items.quote: Yeah. So, generally, if the price is ₹50, then ₹50 is to the channel partner, then it will be ₹100 to the end user. And from that, they will give the discount or something like that. And our cost is 40%. So gross margin is 60%.

items.statement: Khushi Paun joined as management trainee in Mumbai; expected to relocate to Dubai within 3 months
items.quote: She joined to Mumbai office last month only. And, hopefully, she will shift to Dubai within three months.

items.statement: Hiring Head of System Integrator partnerships in UAE to onboard 100+ partners
items.quote: Also, the system integrator, so we are hiring one Head especially for the system integrator from the community only. So that Head will set up system integrator partnerships with more than 100 people, within these years and UAE and GCC.

items.statement: Revenue grew 18% YoY to ₹63 crores in FY25; gross sales ₹71.15 crores
items.quote: And last year, we did ₹53 crores to ₹63 crores. So it is almost 18% growth. And gross sales we did ₹71.15 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA grew from ₹7.14 crores to ₹7.56 crores in FY25
items.quote: And last year, we did ₹7.14 crores to ₹7.56 crores. So EBITDA, amount wise its increased.

items.statement: 10x growth path requires sustained high investment in people, events, marketing; margins may stay near current levels during growth phase
items.quote: 10x, the journey may always require to do such activities. So we are not in the way of the burning or something like that. But yes, definitely this year maybe 12% to 13% we may achieve.

items.statement: Transfer pricing between India and Dubai at arm's length; India manufactures, sells to Dubai at wholesale margin
items.quote: So, there's a very clear transparent policy in the company that, Marvel will take the margin what they should get to sell that to Callistus. So let's say the cost is ₹100 and to Dubai to ₹120, because those kind of things count is a wholesale pricing.

items.statement: Management declined to provide revenue, EBITDA or PAT margin guidance for FY26 or next 2-3 years citing UPSI/compliance
items.quote: We cannot give any kind of guidance. Sorry.

items.statement: Spices capacity utilization at 65% with 35% headroom; atta at ~88% utilization; oil plant not yet utilized
items.quote: Utilization of spices is done with 65% only. So overall, if we go for this utilization, go through the utilization, these numbers, it's growth drivers enough for us for this financials and we don't need any expansion.

items.statement: Spices installed capacity 3,600 tons/annum (2,637 tons utilized); atta 14,400 tons/annum (12,650 tons utilized); oil 7,200 tons/annum not yet commercialized
items.quote: For spices and masalas, we have an installed capacity of 3,600 tons per annum with the current utilization at about 2,637 tons. When it comes to atta, 14,400 tons per annum installed capacity and we have utilized 12,650 tons. Regarding oil, we have installed capacity of 7,200 tons per annum but this plant is yet to be commercialized.

items.statement: Revenue split: masalas 49%, atta 55% (overlap noted); oil launched May 10, 2025; Poushtik 500 SKUs (35% in-house, 45% white-label Srivari, 20-25% outsourced)
items.quote: Our revenue is almost evenly split between two core product categories; masalas contributing 49% and atta contributing 55% and we launched our edible oil on 10th May 2025 and it started its commercial production on 10th May 2025.

items.statement: Poushtik cart value INR800-1,000 vs industry INR400-600; operational cost at 25% of quick commerce platforms; no discount strategy
items.quote: Generally if you go through the cart value of the application or the other e-commerce platform is around INR400 to INR600 any other -- all the platforms, but our cart value will be more than INR900 to INR1,000 in between we are assuming that exactly as per our research, so it will be minimum of INR800 to INR1,000.

items.statement: Spices/masalas margin 35-40%; pulses/grains margin 30-35%; oil/ghee margin 18-22%; PAT decreased due to 6-month depreciation claim on new oil plant
items.quote: Our PAT has been decreased. See PAT has been decreased due to the new plant commencement and we have claimed the depreciation of the 6 months because of that PAT has been decreased, but our overall numbers are positive.

items.statement: B2B tie-ups with DMart, Jumbotail (2 lakh stores), BigBasket, Udaan; 29 Ushodaya stores, 13 Balaji Grand Bazar outlets; expanding to Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Odisha via Jumbotail
items.quote: We have successfully placed our products on a new e-commerce limited online portal that is DMart and also successfully placed on our products in 29 Ushodaya supermarket stores across Hyderabad and Secunderabad and captured consumer's base at 13 premium large format outlets at Balaji Grand Bazar.

items.statement: Bank working capital facility INR12 cr (INR2 cr additional); fully utilized; can double to INR24 cr based on financials; Poushtik is 100% cash-and-carry needing minimal funding
items.value: INR12 cr facility, INR2 cr additional
items.quote: INR12 crores is a facility, INR200 lakhs is a facility with the banking. So we can move further. We can fund from the banking also. And parallelly, we will be -- as of now we are not looking any fundraise for the next, this H1.

items.statement: Rights issue funds fully utilized per letter of offer: INR8.64 cr oil plant, INR1.90 cr unsecured loan repayment, INR10 cr working capital, INR4 cr general corporate
items.quote: As disclosed in the letter of offer, we have utilized the entire amount for the specified purpose without any deviation.

items.statement: Oil plant capex INR17.5 cr (incl. working capital) vs INR8 cr in offer letter; 20% cost increase due to civil works and advanced automated export-oriented technology
items.quote: So, parallel that is including that working capital is included in that, that INR17.5 crores as a Company Secretary had mentioned and delay was because of we have invested more into this infrastructure as it is a civil work was huge in this setup plant.

items.statement: Export operations to start in H2 FY26; no revenue guidance provided
items.quote: See, there is no, not a plan for the revenues and these numbers of the exports, but definitely we are the second, H2, we are going to start the export.

items.statement: India spices market >INR2 lakh cr; 70% unorganized shifting to organized by 2030; atta similarly 70% loose/unorganized
items.quote: As I said, one important thing is in the spices, still 70% is an unorganized trade. So, after the post COVID, now people are moving to the packaging and quality products. So, 70% will now come down by 2030, we are expecting 70% will be the organized trade.

items.statement: Competing on quality at competitive price; entering new states via B2B platforms (Jumbotail, Kirana stores) focusing on general trade first with small ticket sizes INR1,000-3,000
items.quote: So, we, our strategy to compete with them is we see, first of all, is our is a high quality product, but competitive price and we start with the small placements, small stores focus initially. So, we will focus in the general trade, not in the modern trade initially

items.statement: Chillies sourced from Guntur, Khammam, Warangal, Raichur, Malakpet, Hyderabad; wheat from Sehore, Vidisha, Sironj (MP); groundnut sourced within 50 km radius of Telangana factory
